area: Rio Grande do Sul state / Porto Alegre metropolitan region, including Canoas

entries.headline: Civil Defense issues meteorological alert for storms and intense rain
entries.detail: Rio Grande do Sul state Civil Defense warns of risk of disruption from isolated storms and locally intense rain, with possible flooding and power cuts.
entries.source: Wikipedia, "2024 Rio Grande do Sul floods" (summarizing state Civil Defense bulletins)

entries.headline: First storm system hits the Vale do Rio Pardo region
entries.detail: Strong storms bringing high winds and torrential rain begin sweeping into Rio Grande do Sul state.
entries.source: "Analyzing the Effect of an Extreme Weather Event on Telecommunications and IT: Insights from 30 Days of Flooding" (PAM 2025 preprint)

entries.headline: Red alert issued as rain spreads across almost the entire state
entries.detail: Heavy rain and strong winds that began in the north on April 28 spread to nearly the whole state by April 29; a red alert is issued.
entries.source: Wikipedia, "2024 Rio Grande do Sul floods"; corroborated by the PAM 2025 preprint above

entries.headline: INMET reports over 150 mm of rain in 24 hours in parts of the state
entries.detail: Brazil's national meteorological institute (INMET) records more than 150 mm of rainfall within 24 hours in parts of Rio Grande do Sul.
entries.source: Wikipedia, "2024 Rio Grande do Sul floods", citing INMET

entries.headline: Guaíba river gauge breaks the 1941 flood record
entries.detail: The Guaíba gauge in Porto Alegre, a few kilometres from Canoas, reaches 4.77 m, surpassing the historic 1941 flood record of 4.76 m.

entries.headline: Canoas residents evacuated by boat and human chain
entries.detail: The mayor of Canoas calls for boat owners to assist with search-and-rescue; residents stand shoulder-deep in water and form human chains to pull boats carrying people to safety.
entries.source: Associated Press, via Washington Post photo coverage

entries.headline: Guaíba hits a new historical peak; state-wide death toll rises sharply
entries.detail: The Guaíba reaches a new record level (independently reported as 5.33-5.35 m by different outlets) on Sunday morning. At least 75 dead and 103 missing are reported state-wide, with more than 88,000 people displaced.

entries.headline: Sentinel-2 captures this case study's cloud-free signal scene over Canoas
entries.detail: This is the satellite pass this app uses to detect new water. By this date, archived alerts had already stood at "emergency" level for three days.
entries.source: Copernicus / Sentinel-2 L2A, tile T22JDN (see data/manifest.json)

note: Manually curated from public weather-service and news reporting published at the time, each entry cited with its own source and retrieval date. No live news or weather API is called by this app; this is a fixed, archived record used to demonstrate that monitoring public alerts would have flagged this area for satellite tasking before the imagery confirmed flooding.
numeric_discrepancy_note: Independent outlets reported slightly different Guaíba gauge readings and dates for the same rise (e.g. 4.77 m on May 3 vs. 5.31 m on May 4 vs. 5.33-5.35 m on May 5, across different sources). This app does not reconcile these into one canonical number; each charted level_m value is exactly the figure reported by that entry's own cited source, nothing averaged or interpolated.

historical_record.label: 1941 flood record (pre-2024)
historical_record.source: Reported consistently across the cited outlets (Wikipedia, Al Jazeera, PAM 2025 preprint) as the record the 2024 flood surpassed.

summary: Archived alerts for this area first reached 'advisory' level on 2024-04-22, 14 day(s) before the satellite signal scene used in this case study (2024-05-06), and reached 'emergency' level on 2024-05-03, 3 day(s) before that scene. In a live deployment, this kind of feed -- not the satellite -- is what would trigger tasking a fresh image of this area in the first place.
